notes: Five adversarial rounds, the first four DISAGREE, each finding a real silent bypass -- exit 0 with no error on a workflow that genuinely runs a self-hosted job. Round 1: strategy.matrix.include, mainstream documented syntax the check never inspected. Round 2: a flow mapping as a sequence item, where splitting on the first colon produced the key '{os'. Round 3: the same flow mapping wrapped across two lines, which fell through the same-line guard back into the naive split. Round 4: a YAML anchor prefix, '&x os: self-hosted', whose garbage key carries no flow delimiter and so slipped past the character blocklist added in round 3. Rounds 2 to 4 are the same bug in four spellings, and the reviewer's diagnosis of why is the reason this reached AGREE: head.partition(':') assumed a sequence item's head was already a clean key-value pair, when YAML lets it carry anchors, aliases, tags and flow openers first, so each round of blocklisting one more character found one more spelling. The fix is now an allowlist -- the only head grammar this reader claims to understand -- and everything else fails closed by construction, which is what the module docstring already promised. Round 5 attacked that grammar directly with leading digits, unicode, quoting edge cases, whitespace and decoy values, could not get through it, found no over-rejection for realistic GitHub Actions keys, re-ran 44 accumulated cases with no regressions, and said plainly it would merge. Its one remaining finding, that the sequence-item head-plus-nested merge bypassed the new duplicate-key guard, is fixed in this PR rather than deferred. Also fixed across the rounds: a false positive on the real hosted label windows-11-arm, a false rejection of a legitimate workflow whose run block contained a --- line, and two multi-document merge spellings. macos-26 was deliberately left out of the label allow-list: the flag was moderate-confidence from a secondary source, and a false accept is the wrong direction to guess in.
